appearance.addEffect.description: Applies a live effect with its parameters to the targets or one of their appearance items (the same as effect.apply).

appearance.addFill.description: Adds a new fill on top of each selected object's appearance stack, copied from its top fill.

appearance.addStroke.description: Adds a new stroke on top of each selected object's appearance stack, copied from its top stroke.

appearance.clear.description: Clears each selected object's appearance to one empty fill and stroke and resets its opacity and blend mode.

appearance.copyFrom.description: Copies the appearance of object source onto ids or the selection, as the Eyedropper does, with options for what is picked up and applied.

appearance.duplicateItem.description: Duplicates appearance items (fills or strokes with their effects) in each target's stack, by default right above the original.

appearance.moveItem.description: Moves an appearance item to another position in the targets' paint order.

appearance.newArt.description: Answers the appearance, opacity, blend and graphic style the next object drawn will get.

appearance.reduceToBasic.description: Keeps only the topmost visible fill and stroke of each selected object and drops extra items and effects.

appearance.removeItem.description: Removes fills or strokes by index from each target object's appearance stack.

appearance.setActiveItem.description: Chooses which appearance item of the first selected object later paint, stroke and effect commands target when they omit item.

appearance.setItem.description: Edits one fill or stroke item of the targets' appearance stacks by index: its paint, opacity, blend, visibility or weight.

appearance.setNewArtBasic.description: Sets whether new art gets a basic appearance (one fill and stroke) or the last selected object's whole appearance.

appearance.showAllHidden.description: Makes every hidden fill, stroke and effect of the selected objects visible again; answers the ids changed.

appearance.targetContents.description: Selects the members of the selected groups and layers so later appearance edits apply to them, as double-clicking Contents does; answers the ids.

appearance.transfer.description: Gives target the appearance and transparency of source (moving it, or copying with copy), as dragging a Layers panel target circle does.

artboard.convertToArtboards.description: Turns each selected object's bounds into a new artboard, removing the objects.

artboard.copy.description: Copies an artboard (and optionally its art) to the clipboard so a paste adds it again here or in another document.

artboard.cut.description: Copies an artboard (and optionally its art) to the clipboard, then deletes it and that art in one undo step.

artboard.delete.description: Deletes the artboard at index; its art stays on the canvas.

artboard.duplicate.description: Duplicates an artboard to the right of the last one, optionally with copies of the art fully inside it.

artboard.fitToArt.description: Resizes an artboard to the visible art's bounds (strokes and effects included).

artboard.fitToSelection.description: Resizes an artboard to the bounds of the selected art.

artboard.move.description: Moves an artboard by dx, dy with the art fully inside it (or leaves it and moves copies with copy).

artboard.new.description: Adds an artboard at a position and size (default right of the last one) with an optional name.

artboard.rearrange.description: Rearranges all artboards in a grid, row or column with an order, column count and spacing, optionally moving their art.

artboard.reorder.description: Changes an artboard's number in the artboard order.

artboard.setProps.description: Changes an artboard's name, position or size, optionally moving or scaling the art inside it.

assets.add.description: Collects the selected art as assets for asset export, one per object or one for all; answers the assets.

assets.export.description: Exports each asset's art, cropped to it, in every format row of the export settings, to a folder or zip.

assets.list.description: Answers the Asset Export panel's assets with their objects and bounds.

assets.remove.description: Removes assets from the Asset Export panel (their art stays).

assets.rename.description: Renames an asset, which names its exported files.

assets.settings.set.description: Changes the export settings the Asset Export panel and Export for Screens share.

attributes.info.description: Answers the Attributes panel values of the selection: overprint, centre point, image map, URL, note, fill rule and path direction.

attributes.set.description: Sets Attributes panel values on the selection: overprint fill and stroke, centre point display, image map, URL and note.

brush.apply.description: Applies a brush to the strokes of the selected or given paths (adding a stroke if missing) and makes it current.

brush.delete.description: Deletes a brush; strokes using it become plain strokes.

brush.duplicate.description: Duplicates a brush under a new name and answers it.

brush.freehand.description: Paints a freehand stroke along points with a brush, as the Paintbrush does; answers its id.

brush.get.description: Answers one brush's full definition as JSON.

brush.list.description: Answers the document's brushes with their types and the current brush.

brush.new.description: Creates a calligraphic, scatter, art, pattern or bristle brush, from parameters or the selected art; answers its name.

brush.options.description: Changes a brush's definition fields (see brush.get); out-of-range values are clamped.

brush.remove.description: Removes brushes from the selected strokes, leaving plain strokes.

brush.setCurrent.description: Sets the brush the Paintbrush paints with; not an undo step.

charStyle.apply.description: Applies a character style to the selection, ids or a byte range, optionally clearing overrides; answers how many runs changed.

charStyle.delete.description: Deletes a character style; text using it keeps its look.

charStyle.duplicate.description: Duplicates a character style under a new name and answers it.

charStyle.list.description: Answers the document's character styles with their attributes and how many runs use each.

charStyle.new.description: Creates a character style from attributes or the selected text's; answers its name.

charStyle.redefine.description: Redefines a character style from the selected text; text using it updates and keeps its overrides.

charStyle.setAttrs.description: Replaces a character style's attributes; text using it updates and keeps its overrides.

clipboard.conflicts.description: Answers the global or spot swatches on the clipboard whose names the active document gives another colour, so you can pass swatchConflict to a paste.

clipboard.exportPdf.description: Answers the clipboard's objects as a one-page PDF sized to their visual bounds, or null when the clipboard is empty.

clipboard.exportPng.description: Answers the clipboard's objects as a PNG cropped to their visual bounds with a transparent background, at scale pixels per point.

clipboard.exportSvg.description: Answers the clipboard's objects as standalone SVG markup, or null when the clipboard is empty; the document is unchanged.

clipboard.exportText.description: Answers the copied type objects' text, one object per line, or null unless every copied object is type.

clipboard.flavours.description: Answers the MIME types Copy offers other applications for the current clipboard, best first, according to the clipboard preferences.

clipboard.importEmf.description: Replaces the kit's clipboard with the paths, images and type of an EMF or WMF picture; unsupported records are skipped with a warning. Run edit.paste afterwards.

clipboard.importImage.description: Replaces the kit's clipboard with an embedded image from PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, TIFF or BMP bytes at its physical size; run edit.paste afterwards.

clipboard.importPdf.description: Replaces the kit's clipboard with the objects of one page of a PDF (with its images and swatches); run edit.paste afterwards.

clipboard.importSvg.description: Replaces the kit's clipboard with the objects of SVG markup or SVG/SVGZ bytes, centred on center; run edit.pasteInPlace afterwards to place them.

clipboard.importText.description: Replaces the kit's clipboard with point text of the given text in the default type style; run edit.paste afterwards.

color.convert.description: Converts a colour to RGB, CMYK, grey or Lab through the working spaces and answers its values, hex and whether it is out of gamut.

color.gamutCheck.description: Answers the colours of the selection (or document) that can't print in the working CMYK, with how far out and how often used.

color.harmony.description: Answers a colour harmony (complementary, triad, analogous, shades and more) built from a base colour, optionally snapped to a swatch library; changes nothing.

color.loadProfile.description: Registers an ICC colour profile from a file (native app only) so it can be used as a working space; answers its name and kind.

color.plates.description: Answers the document's ink plates (process and spot) and which are visible in Separations Preview.

colorTheme.addToSwatches.description: Adds a saved theme's colours to the swatches as a colour group named after it.

colorTheme.list.description: Answers the saved colour themes with their colours and harmony rules.

colorTheme.save.description: Saves a colour theme of 1 to 5 colours (or one made from a colour and a harmony rule), optionally replacing a saved theme.

command.batch.description: Runs a list of commands as one undo step and stops at the first error, rolling everything back; use it for multi-step edits that must succeed together.

css.export.description: Writes CSS for the selection or all objects to a file, optionally rasterizing pictures its rules refer to.

css.generate.description: Answers CSS rules for every object in the document.

css.selection.description: Answers CSS rules for the selected objects (fills, strokes, type, opacity, optionally positions and sizes) in a unit.

dataset.capture.description: Records what the bound objects hold now as a new dataset and makes it active.

dataset.list.description: Answers the datasets with their values, the active one, and which the art still matches.

dataset.new.description: Adds a dataset with values per variable.

dataset.next.description: Applies the next dataset, wrapping around.

dataset.prev.description: Applies the previous dataset, wrapping around.

dataset.rename.description: Renames a dataset, keeping its values.

dataset.select.description: Applies a dataset's values to the bound objects in one undo step; answers what was applied and skipped.

dataset.set.description: Replaces a dataset's values; variables left out lose their value in it.

dataset.update.description: Writes what the bound objects hold now into the active dataset.

document.activate.description: Makes the open document at index the active one, so later commands act on it.

document.dxfInfo.description: Answers what a DXF drawing holds (version, units, layouts, layers, default scale) without opening it.

document.export.description: Writes the document, its selection or chosen artboards to a file in a format (SVG, PDF, PNG, JPEG, TIFF, PSD, DXF, EPS and more) with that format's options, or answers the data when no path is given. Never changes the document's own path.

document.exportBytes.description: Answers the document, its selection or chosen artboards as a file in a format (SVG, PDF, PNG, JPEG, TIFF, PSD, DXF, EPS and more) with document.export's options, as base64 `data` (with `files` when the format writes one file per artboard), without writing a file or changing the document: the host writes it.

document.exportDxf.description: Writes the document as a DXF drawing with a version, unit, scale and colour depth, or answers the data.

document.exportEps.description: Writes the document as EPS with a PostScript level, preview and transparency options, or answers the data.

document.exportForOffice.description: Writes one artboard as a PNG at a chosen resolution for office documents and slides, or answers its data when no path is given.

document.exportForScreens.description: Exports each chosen artboard or asset in one or more formats and sizes (as the Export for Screens dialog does), to a folder or a zip; answers the files written. Remembers the settings in the document.

document.exportForWeb.description: Writes an optimised GIF, JPEG or PNG for the web with a preset and settings (colours, dither, quality, size), or answers the data.

document.exportForWeb.preview.description: Answers what Save for Web would write: file size, colours and download time, optionally with the image data.

document.exportPdf.description: Writes the document's artboards as a PDF with a preset or options (standard, compression, marks, bleed, layers, security), or answers the data.

document.exportSelection.description: Exports only the selected objects, cropped to their bounds, as PNG, JPEG, WebP, SVG or PDF; answers the file or its data with the bounds.

document.exportSettings.description: Answers the Export for Screens settings the document last exported with, or {} when it never was.

document.find.description: Searches the document's objects by Layers panel name, kind or text content and answers the matches with their ids and paths; limit 0 only counts.

document.formats.description: Answers every file format the kit can open or write with its extensions and options, plus formats it cannot handle with what to use instead.

document.info.description: Answers the Document Info report: objects, styles, swatches, patterns, gradients, symbols, fonts and images, for the document or the selection.

document.inspect.description: Answers the active document's layer tree, artboards, selection and history; depth and childLimit slice large trees. Start here before editing, and use document.node for one object.

document.json.description: Answers the complete document model as JSON; large, so prefer document.inspect or document.node unless you need everything.

document.node.description: Answers one object by id: its kind, geometry, paint and children; summary gives a compact form, depth and childLimit bound the children shown.

document.open.description: Opens a file by path or from base64 bytes (native, SVG, PDF, AI, EPS, DXF, images and more) as a new active document; PDF options pick pages, the box and how text comes in.

document.pdfInfo.description: Answers a PDF's page count, page sizes and boxes, and optionally a thumbnail, without opening it; also says whether a password is needed.

document.pdfSettings.description: Answers the PDF settings a preset gives with options applied and how they differ from it, without writing a file.

document.rasterEffectsSettings.description: Sets the document's raster effects settings: resolution, colour model, background, anti-aliasing and clipping mask.

document.save.description: Saves the document to its own file or to path in a format (native, template, PDF, SVG, AI) with that format's options; without a known path it answers the data and stays modified.

document.serialize.description: Answers the active document as file data in a format (native by default, SVG, PDF, raster and more) without writing a file or changing the document.

document.setUnits.description: Sets the document's units, which every length the editor shows and reads uses; drawing coordinates passed to commands stay in points.

document.setup.description: Sets Document Setup options: units, bleed, outline images, font substitution highlighting, transparency grid, type options and language.

edit.assignProfile.description: Tags the document with RGB and/or CMYK profiles without changing colour numbers.

edit.clear.description: Deletes the objects ids, else the selection (direct-selected anchors, else whole objects, else selected ruler guides).

edit.colorSettings.description: Sets the RGB and CMYK working spaces, rendering intent and black point compensation; answers them with the available profiles.

edit.colors.adjustBalance.description: Shifts the selection's colours by per-channel amounts in RGB, CMYK, grey or global tint mode; answers how many changed.

edit.colors.blendFrontToBack.description: Grades the fills of three or more selected objects between the frontmost and backmost colours.

edit.colors.blendHorizontally.description: Grades the fills of three or more selected objects between the leftmost and rightmost colours.

edit.colors.blendVertically.description: Grades the fills of three or more selected objects between the topmost and bottommost colours.

edit.colors.invert.description: Inverts the colours of the selection or ids in fills, strokes, text, meshes, embedded images and pattern tiles.

edit.colors.overprintBlack.description: Makes the black fills and/or strokes of the selection overprint (or stops them), optionally including rich and spot blacks.

edit.colors.saturate.description: Increases or decreases the saturation of the selection's colours by an intensity percentage; answers how many changed.

edit.colors.toCMYK.description: Converts the colours of the selection or ids to CMYK; answers how many changed.

edit.colors.toGrayscale.description: Converts the colours of the selection or ids to greyscale; answers how many changed.

edit.colors.toRGB.description: Converts the colours of the selection or ids to RGB; answers how many changed.

edit.copy.description: Copies the selection to the kit's clipboard without changing the document (with the Artboard tool chosen, the active artboard and its art).

edit.cut.description: Removes the selection and puts it on the kit's clipboard (with the Artboard tool chosen, the active artboard and its art).

edit.duplicate.description: Duplicates the selection in place, optionally offset by dx/dy, and selects the copies.

edit.findNext.description: Selects the next type object containing find, after the selected one; answers its id or null.

edit.findReplace.description: Finds and replaces text in every type object (or ids), optionally matching case and whole words; answers the count replaced.

edit.paste.description: Pastes the clipboard's objects and the resources they use, centred on center or offset by dx/dy; answers the new ids and any resources added, merged or renamed. Use pasteInPlace to keep their positions.

edit.pasteInBack.description: Pastes the clipboard in place just below the bottom selected object, or at the bottom of the current layer; answers the new ids.

edit.pasteInFront.description: Pastes the clipboard in place just above the top selected object, or on top of the current layer; answers the new ids.

edit.pasteInPlace.description: Pastes the clipboard at the exact positions the objects were copied from; answers the new ids.

edit.pasteOnAllArtboards.description: Pastes a copy of the clipboard on every artboard at the offset the objects had to their original artboard; answers the new ids.

edit.pasteWithoutFormatting.description: Pastes like edit.paste, but pasted text takes the default character style and drops its own styles.

edit.redo.description: Redoes the last undone step in a scope (the person's or the agent's; default the caller's).

edit.undo.description: Undoes the last step in a scope (the person's or the agent's; default the caller's), leaving the other scope's later steps in place.

effect.apply.description: Applies a live effect (see effect.list for ids and parameters) to the selection, ids or one appearance item; the effect stays editable.

effect.duplicate.description: Inserts a copy of the effect at index right after it.

effect.expandAppearance.description: Expands each object's appearance into plain objects: every fill and stroke becomes its own object and geometry effects are baked in.

effect.list.description: Answers the catalogue of live effects with their parameters and defaults, and the effects applied to the selection.

effect.move.description: Moves an effect within an effect list or between appearance items.

effect.remove.description: Removes the effect at index from the selection's (or one appearance item's) effect list.

effect.setParams.description: Changes the parameters or visibility of the effect at index on the selection or ids.

eyedropper.setOptions.description: Sets which attributes the Eyedropper picks up and applies and its image sample size; affects appearance.copyFrom.

file.close.description: Closes the document at index (default the active one) without saving; use document.save first to keep changes.

file.closeAll.description: Closes every open document without saving; answers how many closed.

file.documentColorMode.description: Switches the document between CMYK and RGB, converting every colour, symbol, pattern and swatch through the colour settings.

file.formatOptions.description: Answers a writable format's options with their types, defaults and the values the document last saved with, plus the formats Save As offers.

file.info.description: Sets the document's File Info metadata (title, author, description, keywords, rating, copyright) in one undo step.

file.new.description: Creates a new document and makes it active, optionally from a named preset with its own size, units, orientation, artboards, bleed and colour mode; answers the new document's index. Use document.open for an existing file.

file.newFromTemplate.description: Opens a template (or any readable file) as a new untitled document, leaving the template file untouched.

file.newPresets.description: Answers the New Document presets by category (recent, saved, mobile, web, print and more) with their sizes.

file.newPresets.delete.description: Deletes a saved New Document preset.

file.newPresets.save.description: Saves New Document settings as a user preset in the Saved category.

file.package.description: Packages the document with copies of its linked files and fonts into a folder, optionally relinking to the copies, and writes a report.

file.place.description: Places a file (image, PDF page, document or text) into the document at a position or rect, linked or embedded; answers the placed object.

file.place.info.description: Answers what file.place would place from a file (size, resolution, colour mode, warnings, thumbnail) without placing it.

file.place.queue.description: Loads the place cursor with up to 100 files so later clicks place them one by one.

file.print.description: Prints the document by writing a print-ready PDF or PostScript file with the print settings.

file.recovery.discard.description: Deletes recovery copies left by a crash.

file.recovery.list.description: Answers the recovery copies in the store with their titles, paths, formats and whether they belong to open documents.

file.recovery.restore.description: Opens recovery copies left by a crash as new modified documents titled with [Recovered].

file.recovery.save.description: Writes a recovery copy of every modified document changed since its last copy.

file.revert.description: Discards unsaved changes by reloading the document's saved file into the same tab and clearing its history; only for saved, modified documents.

file.saveAs.description: Saves the document to a new path and format, after which the document takes that path, name and format (a template is always a copy).

file.saveAsTemplate.description: Writes the document as a native template that opens as a new untitled document; the document itself is unchanged.

file.saveCopy.description: Writes a copy of the document to path in a format while the document keeps its own path, title and modified state.

flattener.presets.delete.description: Deletes a saved transparency flattener preset (built-in ones stay).

flattener.presets.export.description: Writes transparency flattener presets as a .vcflattener file, or answers its text.

flattener.presets.import.description: Imports transparency flattener presets from a .vcflattener file.

flattener.presets.list.description: Answers the transparency flattener presets, built-in and saved, with their options.

flattener.presets.save.description: Creates or changes a saved transparency flattener preset from options; answers it.

flattener.preview.description: Answers which areas flattening would rasterize, outline or expand, as the Flattener Preview panel highlights them.

gradient.selectStop.description: Selects a stop of the gradient behind the active paint proxy so later stop edits act on it; null clears it.

graph.create.description: Creates a graph (column, bar, line, area, scatter, pie, radar) in a box from series, categories and rows or CSV; answers its id.

graph.setData.description: Replaces a graph's data from series, categories and rows or CSV; without data answers the current data.

graph.setType.description: Changes a graph's type and options: column and cluster width, legend, markers, axes ranges, ticks and labels.

graphicStyle.addFromLibrary.description: Adds graphic styles from a library to the document, optionally applying the first to the selection.

graphicStyle.apply.description: Applies the named graphic style to the selection, ids or a layer, replacing or adding to their appearance.

graphicStyle.breakLink.description: Unlinks the selection or ids from their graphic style while keeping their look.

graphicStyle.delete.description: Deletes graphic styles by name; linked objects keep their look but are unlinked.

graphicStyle.duplicate.description: Duplicates a graphic style under a new unique name and answers it.

graphicStyle.libraries.description: Answers every graphic style library (built-in, user and loaded) with its style count.

graphicStyle.library.description: Answers one graphic style library's styles.

graphicStyle.list.description: Answers every graphic style with its fills, strokes, effects, transparency and the ids of objects linked to it.

graphicStyle.loadLibrary.description: Loads a .vcstyles library or another document's graphic styles so the library panel lists it.

graphicStyle.merge.description: Adds a new graphic style combining the fills, strokes and effects of two or more styles; answers its name.

graphicStyle.move.description: Moves a graphic style to position to in the list.

graphicStyle.new.description: Creates a graphic style from object id or the first selected object's appearance and transparency; answers its name.

graphicStyle.redefine.description: Replaces a graphic style with the look of object id or the first selected object; every linked object updates.

graphicStyle.rename.description: Renames a graphic style; linked objects stay linked.

graphicStyle.saveLibrary.description: Saves the document's graphic styles as a .vcstyles library file, optionally into the user library folder.

graphicStyle.setOptions.description: Sets whether applying a graphic style to type replaces its characters' own fill and stroke; answers the setting.

graphicStyle.sortByName.description: Sorts the graphic styles by name, keeping the default style first.

graphicStyle.unused.description: Answers the names of graphic styles no object is linked to, without changing anything.

guide.add.description: Adds a vertical or horizontal ruler guide at a position, across the canvas or one artboard, on a layer.

guide.list.description: Answers the ruler guides with their orientation, position, selection, artboard and layer.

guide.move.description: Moves ruler guide index to a position, or the selected guides by dx/dy, optionally as copies.

guide.remove.description: Deletes ruler guide index, else the selected guides; answers how many.

guide.select.description: Selects ruler guides by index on their own (or toggles them), deselecting art.

guide.setLayer.description: Moves ruler guides (by index or the selected ones) to a layer; answers how many.

image.info.description: Answers an image object's link, colour mode, pixel size, resolution and placed size.

imageTrace.expand.description: Keeps only the traced paths of Image Trace groups, dropping the source image.

imageTrace.make.description: Traces an embedded image into vector paths with a preset or parameters (mode, threshold, colours, paths, corners, noise); the result stays live.

imageTrace.makeAndExpand.description: Traces an image like imageTrace.make and expands the result into plain paths; answers the counts.

imageTrace.presets.description: Answers the Image Trace presets with their parameters.

imageTrace.release.description: Puts the source image back in place of Image Trace groups.

imageTrace.setView.description: Sets how Image Trace objects draw on screen (result, outlines, source image); exports keep the tracing result.

layer.clippingMask.toggle.description: Makes (or releases) a layer-level clipping mask: the layer's or group's top object clips the rest of it.

layer.collectInNew.description: Moves the given rows (or the selected objects) into a new layer where the topmost of them was; answers its id.

layer.delete.description: Deletes Layers panel rows (layers, sublayers, groups or objects) with what they hold; the last layer always stays.

layer.duplicate.description: Duplicates Layers panel rows, each copy just above its original; answers the copies' ids.

layer.flatten.description: Moves the art of every other visible top-level layer into one layer, deleting hidden layers; template layers stay.

layer.hideOthers.description: Hides every top-level layer except those holding the highlighted rows (or the current layer).

layer.highlight.description: Highlights Layers panel rows (set, add or toggle); the last one's layer becomes current. Not an undo step.

layer.locate.description: Highlights an object's row in the Layers panel and answers its ancestry of layers; the document is unchanged.

layer.lockOthers.description: Locks every top-level layer except those holding the highlighted rows (or the current layer).

layer.merge.description: Merges two or more highlighted rows into the last one, keeping stacking order and removing emptied layers; answers its id.

layer.move.description: Moves (or copies) Layers panel rows above, below or inside a target row, as dragging in the panel does.

layer.new.description: Adds a layer directly above the current layer (or on top of all layers) with optional name, colour, template, lock, visibility and print options; answers its id.

layer.newSublayer.description: Adds a sublayer on top of a layer's contents (default the current layer); answers its id.

layer.outlineOthers.description: Turns every other top-level layer into outline view, keeping the highlighted ones in preview.

layer.pasteRemembersLayers.description: Sets (or toggles) whether pasting puts objects back into the layers they were copied from.

layer.previewAll.description: Turns preview on for every layer and sublayer; answers how many changed.

layer.releaseToLayers.description: Moves each object of a layer or group into its own new sublayer, in stacking order (build stacks them cumulatively for animation).

layer.releaseToLayersBuild.description: Releases a layer's objects into sublayers that build up cumulatively (each sublayer holds one more object); answers the new ids.

layer.reverse.description: Reverses the stacking order of two or more rows that share a layer or group.

layer.selectAll.description: Selects the visible, unlocked art of a layer (or the object itself), or adds it to the selection, as the Layers panel's selection column does.

layer.setCurrent.description: Highlights one Layers panel row and makes its layer the current layer where new art goes; not an undo step.

layer.setProps.description: Sets layer options on rows: name, visibility, lock, template, printing, preview, image dimming and colour.

layer.showAll.description: Shows every layer and sublayer; answers how many changed.

layer.target.description: Targets a layer, group or object as clicking its target circle does, so appearance edits apply to it as a whole.

layer.template.description: Turns layers into templates (locked, dimmed, left out of print and export) or back into ordinary layers.

layer.unlockAll.description: Unlocks every layer and sublayer; answers how many changed.

library.add.description: Adds an item from the selection to a library: a graphic, a fill or stroke colour, or a character or paragraph style.

library.create.description: Creates a new empty library and makes it current; answers its id and name.

library.createGroup.description: Creates a group of library items, moving the given items into it.

library.delete.description: Deletes a library and its file; not undoable.

library.deleteGroup.description: Deletes a library group; its items stay in the library ungrouped.

library.export.description: Writes a library as a .vclibrary file, or answers its text.

library.get.description: Answers one library's graphics (with thumbnails), colours, character and paragraph styles and groups.

library.import.description: Adds the library of a .vclibrary file as a new current library.

library.list.description: Answers the shared libraries with counts of their graphics, colours and styles, and the current library.

library.moveItem.description: Moves a library item into a group, or out of its group.

library.removeItem.description: Deletes an item from a library.

library.rename.description: Renames a library (default the current one).

library.renameGroup.description: Renames a group in a library.

library.setCurrent.description: Sets which library the Libraries panel shows and library commands without a library act on.

library.use.description: Uses a library item: places a graphic copy, or applies a colour or style to the selection.

links.check.description: Answers whether each linked file is where it was and whether it changed since it was read.

links.embed.description: Embeds linked images (keeping their pixels) or turns placed documents into editable art, breaking the links.

links.goTo.description: Selects a linked image or placed document and answers its bounds.

links.info.description: Answers an image's or placed document's Link Info: file, status, format, colour mode, size and effective resolution.

links.list.description: Answers every image and placed document as the Links panel lists them, filtered and sorted.

links.placementOptions.description: Sets how linked art fits its bounds when the file is updated or relinked: preserve transforms, bounds, file size, fit or fill, with alignment.

links.relink.description: Links images or placed documents to another file, or each to a same-named file in a folder.

links.unembed.description: Writes an embedded image's pixels to a file and links the image to it.

links.update.description: Reads modified linked files again, keeping each object's bounds; answers what was updated and what is missing.

links.updateChanged.description: Reads again every linked file that changed on disk since it was last seen.

livePaint.expand.description: Turns Region Paint groups into plain groups of their painted faces and edges.

livePaint.fill.description: Fills the Region Paint face containing a point with a colour, swatch, gradient or none.

livePaint.info.description: Answers a Region Paint group's faces with their fills and edges with their strokes.

livePaint.make.description: Builds a Region Paint group from the selected paths so faces and edges can be painted; answers its id and counts.

livePaint.merge.description: Adds the other selected paths and groups to the first Region Paint group, keeping its paint.

livePaint.release.description: Replaces Region Paint groups with their original paths.

livePaint.strokeEdge.description: Paints the Region Paint edge nearest a point with a stroke colour, swatch or none and a width.

magicWand.options.description: Answers the current Magic Wand settings: which attributes it compares and their tolerances.

magicWand.set.description: Changes the Magic Wand settings (which attributes to compare and their tolerances) and answers the settings; affects only select.magicWand.

node.move.description: Puts a row at an index (0 = bottom) inside a parent layer or group, or at the top level.

object.align.description: Aligns the selected objects horizontally and/or vertically to the selection, the artboard or the key object, using preview or geometric bounds.

object.arrange.bringForward.description: Moves the selected objects one step up in the stacking order.

object.arrange.bringToFront.description: Moves the selected objects to the top of their layer's stacking order.

object.arrange.sendBackward.description: Moves the selected objects one step down in the stacking order.

object.arrange.sendToBack.description: Moves the selected objects to the bottom of their layer's stacking order.

object.arrange.sendToCurrentLayer.description: Moves the selected objects to the top of the current layer.

object.blend.expand.description: Expands the selected blends into groups of their keys and generated steps; answers the ids.

object.blend.info.description: Answers the options of the first selected blend (spacing, steps, distance, orientation, keys, spine), else the defaults new blends get.

object.blend.make.description: Blends the selected objects with a number of steps or a distance (or smooth colour) along the page or a path.

object.blend.options.description: Sets spacing (smooth, steps or distance) and orientation of the selected blends, or the defaults for new blends when none is selected.

object.blend.release.description: Releases the selected blends: the key objects come back and the spine stays as an unpainted path below them.

object.blend.replaceSpine.description: Uses the selected path as the spine of the selected blend; the path is consumed.

object.blend.reverseFrontToBack.description: Reverses the stacking order of the selected blends' steps.

object.blend.reverseSpine.description: Reverses the order of the key objects along the selected blend's spine.

object.blend.spine.addAnchor.description: Adds a point to a blend's spine where it passes nearest x, y; answers its index.

object.blend.spine.moveAnchor.description: Moves a point of a blend's spine, or one of its handles, to x, y.

object.blend.spine.removeAnchor.description: Deletes a spine point that no key object sits on.

object.clippingMask.editContents.description: Selects the clipped art inside the selected clip groups, without changing them; answers how many objects are selected.

object.clippingMask.editMask.description: Selects the clipping paths of the selected clip groups, without changing them; answers how many are selected.

object.clippingMask.make.description: Makes the topmost selected path, compound path or text clip the other selected objects into a clip group; answers the group's id.

object.clippingMask.release.description: Turns the selected clip groups into plain groups, keeping their clipping path as an ordinary object.

object.compoundPath.make.description: Combines the selected paths into one compound path whose overlaps make holes.

object.compoundPath.release.description: Splits the selected compound paths back into separate paths.

object.createObjectMosaic.description: Builds a group of rectangles coloured by the selected image's tile colours (a mosaic), optionally deleting the image.

object.createTrimMarks.description: Draws trim marks around the selection or every artboard, in Roman or Japanese style.

object.cropImage.description: Crops the selected embedded image to a rectangle, its artboard or its non-transparent pixels.

object.distort.description: Warps the selection or ids projectively so its bounds' four corners land on the given points, as Free Distort does.

object.distribute.description: Distributes the selected objects evenly by their left, centre or right (or top, centre or bottom) edges.

object.distributeSpacing.description: Spaces the selected objects evenly along an axis, or by a fixed spacing from the key object.

object.envelope.editContents.description: Switches the selected envelopes between editing their contents and editing the envelope itself.

object.envelope.expand.description: Replaces the selected envelopes with groups of their distorted content (type outlined); answers the ids.

object.envelope.info.description: Answers the selected envelope's type and settings, or the defaults new envelopes get.

object.envelope.makeWithMesh.description: Wraps the selected objects in a mesh envelope of rows by columns patches; answers its id.

object.envelope.makeWithTopObject.description: Makes the topmost selected path the envelope of the other selected objects; answers its id.

object.envelope.makeWithWarp.description: Wraps the selected objects in a warp envelope of a style (arc, wave, flag, fisheye…) with bend and distortion; answers the envelope's id.

object.envelope.options.description: Sets envelope options of the selection: fidelity, anti-aliasing, shape preservation and whether appearance, gradients and patterns distort.

object.envelope.release.description: Releases the selected envelopes into their content and their shape (a mesh or the top path); answers the ids.

object.envelope.resetWithMesh.description: Turns the selected envelopes into mesh envelopes of rows by columns, keeping their content.

object.envelope.resetWithWarp.description: Turns the selected envelopes into warp envelopes with a style and bend, keeping their content.

object.envelope.setMeshPoint.description: Moves a point of a mesh envelope (with its handles), or one handle end, to x, y.

object.exitIsolation.description: Leaves isolation mode so edits apply to the whole document again; the document is unchanged.

object.expand.description: Expands the selected objects, fills and/or strokes into plain art: type to outlines, live shapes to paths, effects baked, blends and envelopes to their content.

object.expand.info.description: Answers what each Expand option (object, fill, stroke) would change in the selection.

object.expandBrush.description: Replaces brushed paths in the selection with groups of their brush art.

object.expandShape.description: Converts the selected live shapes (rectangles, ellipses, polygons with corner widgets) into plain editable paths.

object.flattenTransparency.description: Flattens transparency in the selected art into opaque vector and raster pieces with a flattener preset or options.

object.group.description: Groups the selected objects into one group in place and answers the group's id.

object.hide.description: Hides the selected objects; object.showAll shows them again.

object.hide.above.description: Hides the objects in the same layer that are above and overlap the selection; answers the count.

object.hide.otherLayers.description: Hides every layer that holds no selected object; answers the count.

object.isolate.description: Enters isolation mode on the group or object id so later edits stay inside it; the document is unchanged.

object.liquify.description: Applies a Liquify tool (warp, twirl, pucker, bloat, scallop, crystallize, wrinkle) along a brush stroke of points to the selected art.

object.lock.description: Locks the selected objects so they cannot be selected or edited until unlocked.

object.lock.above.description: Locks the objects in the same layer that are above and overlap the selection; answers the count.

object.lock.otherLayers.description: Locks every layer that holds no selected object; answers the count.

object.makePixelPerfect.description: Snaps each selected object's edges to the pixel grid and rounds stroke weights.

object.maskImage.description: Clips the selected image with a rectangle around it and selects that clipping path for cropping by its handles.

object.mesh.addLine.description: Adds a mesh row and column through x, y to a gradient mesh or mesh envelope; answers the new point's index.

object.mesh.create.description: Converts the selected filled paths into gradient meshes of rows by columns, flat or highlighted at the centre or edge.

object.mesh.deletePoint.description: Deletes the mesh lines through one point of a gradient mesh or mesh envelope.

object.mesh.expand.description: Replaces the selected gradient meshes with groups of flat-coloured pieces; answers the ids.

object.mesh.movePoint.description: Moves a point of a gradient mesh or mesh envelope (with its handles), or one handle end, to x, y.

object.mesh.setPointColor.description: Sets the colour and opacity of one point of a gradient mesh.

object.move.description: Moves the selection by dx, dy points, optionally as a copy.

object.nudge.description: Nudges the selected anchors, else objects, else ruler guides by one keyboard increment in a direction (ten with big), as the arrow keys do.

object.path.addAnchorPoints.description: Adds an anchor midway along every segment of the selected paths without changing their shape.

object.path.cleanUp.description: Deletes stray points, unpainted objects and empty text paths from the document; answers how many were removed.

object.path.divideObjectsBelow.description: Cuts the objects below with the selected path, which is removed; answers the resulting ids.

object.path.offsetPath.description: Adds offset copies of the selected paths, grown (or inset for negative offset) with the chosen joins; answers the new ids.

object.path.outlineStroke.description: Replaces the selected stroked paths with filled outlines of their strokes; answers the new ids.

object.path.simplify.description: Reduces the anchors of the selected paths within a tolerance, keeping corners; answers anchor counts before and after.

object.path.splitIntoGrid.description: Splits each selected shape into a grid of rectangles with rows, columns and gutters; answers the new ids.

object.pathfinder.crop.description: Crops the selected shapes to the topmost one's outline (Pathfinder Crop); answers the resulting ids.

object.pathfinder.divide.description: Divides the selected shapes into all the separate faces their overlaps form (Pathfinder Divide); answers the resulting ids.

object.pathfinder.exclude.description: Keeps the areas where the selected shapes don't overlap (Pathfinder Exclude); answers the resulting ids.

object.pathfinder.intersect.description: Keeps only the area where all selected shapes overlap (Pathfinder Intersect); answers the resulting ids.

object.pathfinder.merge.description: Removes hidden parts and merges touching shapes of the same colour (Pathfinder Merge); answers the resulting ids.

object.pathfinder.minusBack.description: Subtracts the back selected shapes from the frontmost one (Pathfinder Minus Back); answers the resulting ids.

object.pathfinder.minusFront.description: Subtracts the front selected shapes from the backmost one (Pathfinder Minus Front); answers the resulting ids.

object.pathfinder.outline.description: Divides the selected shapes into their edge segments as stroked paths (Pathfinder Outline); answers the resulting ids.

object.pathfinder.trim.description: Removes the hidden parts of the selected filled shapes without merging same colours (Pathfinder Trim); answers the resulting ids.

object.pathfinder.unite.description: Unites the selected shapes into one shape (Pathfinder Unite); answers the resulting ids.

object.pattern.cancel.description: Leaves pattern editing mode, discarding the tile changes.

object.pattern.done.description: Leaves pattern editing mode, saving the tile art into the pattern.

object.pattern.edit.description: Enters pattern editing mode for a pattern (default the selected object's fill pattern).

object.pattern.make.description: Makes a pattern swatch from the selection with a tile type and size, and enters pattern editing mode; answers its name.

object.pattern.saveCopy.description: While editing a pattern, saves the current tile as a new pattern swatch; answers its name.

object.pinWarp.description: Warps the selected art by moving warp pins from their positions to targets (optionally turning around pins).

object.pinWarp.pins.description: Answers (and sets up) the warp pins on the selected art: where each started, where it is now and the turn it holds.

object.rasterize.description: Replaces the selected objects with an embedded raster image at a resolution, background, anti-aliasing and colour model.

object.reflect.description: Mirrors the selection across a vertical, horizontal or angled axis through an origin, optionally as a copy.

object.repeat.expand.description: Replaces the selected repeats with groups of their instances.

object.repeat.grid.description: Makes a grid repeat of the selection with rows, columns and spacing; answers its id.

object.repeat.mirror.description: Makes a mirror repeat of the selection about an axis angle and offset; answers its id.

object.repeat.options.description: Sets the options of the selected repeats (radial instances and angles, grid spacing and flips, mirror angle).

object.repeat.radial.description: Makes a radial repeat of the selection with a number of instances and radius; answers its id.

object.repeat.release.description: Releases the selected repeats back to their source art.

object.resetBoundingBox.description: Squares the bounding box of rotated selected objects back to the page without changing their geometry.

object.rotate.description: Rotates the selection by an angle (or to an absolute angle) about an origin, default its centre, optionally as a copy; answers the ids.

object.scale.description: Scales the selection by sx and sy percent about an origin, optionally as a copy and scaling strokes, corners and patterns.

object.setBounds.description: Sets the selection's position and size as the Transform panel does, about one of nine reference points, optionally keeping proportions and scaling strokes and corners.

object.setLiveShape.description: Edits live shape properties of the selected or given shapes: corner radius and kind per corner, polygon sides and angle, pie start and end angles.

object.setOverprint.description: Makes fills and/or strokes of the selection or one appearance item overprint, or knock out.

object.setProps.description: Sets object properties on ids or the selection: name, visibility, lock, opacity, blend mode, isolation, knockout and custom data attributes.

object.shape.convertToShape.description: Turns selected paths that are rectangles or axis-aligned ellipses into live shapes; answers how many converted.

object.shear.description: Shears the selection by an angle along a horizontal or vertical axis through an origin, optionally as a copy.

object.showAll.description: Shows every hidden object in the document and selects them.

object.slice.clipToArtboard.description: Sets or toggles whether slices are clipped to the artboards.

object.slice.combine.description: Combines two or more selected slices into one user slice over their bounds.

object.slice.create.description: Creates a user slice over a rectangle, as dragging with the Slice tool does.

object.slice.delete.description: Deletes user slices and releases object slices (their objects stay).

object.slice.deleteAll.description: Deletes every user slice and releases every object slice.

object.slice.divide.description: Divides each selected slice into a grid of user slices by count or size.

object.slice.duplicate.description: Duplicates the selected slices as user slices, offset by dx, dy.

object.slice.fromGuides.description: Replaces the user slices with the grid the ruler guides cut the artboards into.

object.slice.fromSelection.description: Creates a user slice over the visual bounds of the selected objects.

object.slice.make.description: Makes each selected object an object slice that follows its bounds.

object.slice.move.description: Moves slices by dx, dy (object slices move their objects).

object.slice.options.description: Sets the selected slices' web options: kind, name, URL, target, message, alt text, cell text, background and alignment.

object.slice.release.description: Releases the selected slices (object slices leave their object; user slices become unpainted rectangles).

object.slice.select.description: Selects slices as the Slice Selection tool does, deselecting objects.

object.slice.setRect.description: Moves or resizes a user slice.

object.textWrap.make.description: Makes area type below the selected objects wrap around them with an offset; answers the ids.

object.textWrap.options.description: Sets the offset and inversion of the selected text-wrap objects, or answers the current options.

object.textWrap.release.description: Stops the selected objects from making text wrap around them; answers the ids.

object.transform.description: Applies an affine matrix to the selection or ids, optionally as a copy and with strokes, corners, type areas and patterns scaling or not.

object.transformAgain.description: Repeats the last move, scale, rotate, reflect, shear or transform on the current selection.

object.transformEach.description: Scales, moves, rotates and reflects each selected object about its own reference point (optionally randomised or as copies), as Transform Each does.

object.ungroup.description: Ungroups the selected groups, leaving their children selected in the same stacking position.

object.unlockAll.description: Unlocks every locked object in the document and selects them.

object.vectorHalftone.description: Converts the selected art into a vector halftone of dots, lines or shapes at a frequency and angle, mono or CMYK.

paint.complement.description: Replaces the active proxy's colours of the selection with their complements, keeping each colour's model.

paint.default.description: Resets the selection or ids and the default paint to a white fill and a 1 pt black stroke (type: black fill, no stroke).

paint.editGradient.description: Sets or edits the gradient on the fill or stroke of the selection: kind (linear, radial, freeform), stops, angle and aspect.

paint.freeform.addLine.description: Joins freeform gradient points with a smooth line along which colour blends.

paint.freeform.addPoint.description: Adds a colour point to the freeform gradient on the selection's fill or stroke at a position, with colour, opacity and spread.

paint.freeform.deletePoint.description: Removes a point from a freeform gradient (never the last one).

paint.freeform.get.description: Answers the freeform gradient behind the first selected object's fill or stroke: its mode, points, lines and selected point.

paint.freeform.selectPoint.description: Selects a freeform gradient point so the Gradient tool and panels act on it; null clears it.

paint.freeform.setPoint.description: Edits a freeform gradient point: position, colour, opacity or spread.

paint.freeform.splitLine.description: Splits a freeform gradient line by adding a point on one of its segments.

paint.invert.description: Inverts the active proxy's (fill's or stroke's) colours of the selection, keeping each colour's model.

paint.lastColor.description: Applies the last solid colour used to the active proxy of the selection and defaults.

paint.lastGradient.description: Applies the last gradient used, fitted to each object, to the active proxy of the selection and defaults.

paint.none.description: Sets whichever of fill or stroke is active to None on the selection and defaults.

paint.proxies.description: Answers the paints the Fill and Stroke proxies show (from the selection or the defaults for new art) and which is active.

paint.recent.description: Answers the recently used colours (newest first) and the last colour and gradient.

paint.sampleColor.description: Samples a colour into the active fill or stroke (and the selection), or into one stop of the gradient behind the proxy.

paint.setFill.description: Sets the fill of the selection or ids (or the default fill) to a colour, a swatch, a gradient, a pattern or none; a global or spot swatch stays linked.

paint.setGradientGeom.description: Moves the selected objects' gradient vector (start, end), radial aspect and focal point, as the Gradient tool does.

paint.setStroke.description: Sets the stroke paint of the selection or ids (or the default stroke) to a colour, a swatch, a gradient, a pattern or none; use stroke.set for weight and dashes.

paint.swap.description: Swaps the fill and stroke of the selection or ids and of the default paint.

paint.toggleActive.description: Brings the Fill or the Stroke proxy forward (or swaps them), which decides what paint.none and swatch clicks change; answers which is active.

paraStyle.apply.description: Applies a paragraph style to the paragraphs of the selection, ids or a byte range, optionally clearing overrides.

paraStyle.delete.description: Deletes a paragraph style; text using it keeps its look.

paraStyle.duplicate.description: Duplicates a paragraph style under a new name and answers it.

paraStyle.list.description: Answers the document's paragraph styles with their attributes and how many paragraphs use each.

paraStyle.new.description: Creates a paragraph style from attributes or the selected text's; answers its name.

paraStyle.redefine.description: Redefines a paragraph style from the selected text; paragraphs using it update.

paraStyle.setAttrs.description: Replaces a paragraph style's attributes; paragraphs using it update and keep their overrides.

path.appendAnchor.description: Appends an anchor with optional handles to the end of the last open subpath of path id, as the Pen tool does.

path.average.description: Moves the direct-selected anchors to their average position horizontally, vertically or both.

path.blob.description: Paints a filled brush shape along points and merges it with touching blobs of the same colour, as the Blob Brush does.

path.close.description: Closes the last open subpath of path id, optionally setting the handle into its first anchor.

path.convertAnchor.description: Converts one anchor to a corner or a smooth point (optionally placing its out handle).

path.convertAnchors.description: Converts the direct-selected anchors to corner points (handles retracted) or smooth points in one undo step.

path.create.description: Creates a path from anchors with optional in/out handles, or from SVG path data, open or closed, with the current paint; answers its id.

path.curvature.description: Creates a smooth path curving through the given points (or replaces path id's geometry), as the Curvature tool does; answers its id.

path.curvatureEdit.description: Edits a path as the Curvature tool does: moves, inserts or extends anchors, or closes it, keeping the curve smooth elsewhere.

path.cutAtAnchors.description: Cuts the paths at their direct-selected anchors, opening closed paths and splitting open ones; answers the ids of the pieces.

path.deleteAnchors.description: Deletes the direct-selected anchors and their segments, opening closed paths at those points.

path.eraseRegion.description: Erases a round-brush stroke along points from the selected (or all) paths, as the Eraser does; answers the resulting ids.

path.eraseSegments.description: Erases the parts of the selected paths under a drag along points, as the Path Eraser does.

path.freehand.description: Draws a freehand path through points (with optional pen pressure), smoothed by fidelity, as the Pencil or Paintbrush does; can extend an existing path.

path.insertAnchor.description: Inserts an anchor on segment segment of subpath subpath of path id at parameter t without changing the path's shape.

path.join.description: Joins two open paths at their nearest (or chosen) ends into one path, or closes a single open path.

path.joinScrub.description: Joins the open-path endpoints a scrub along points passes over, as the Join tool does; answers the joined path's id.

path.knife.description: Cuts the selected (or all) closed shapes along a freehand polyline, as the Knife does; answers the pieces' ids.

path.lineCut.description: Splits the selected paths along the line through two points, extended across the art; answers the pieces.

path.mirrorCut.description: Cuts the selected art along an axis and mirrors the kept side onto the other, as one undo step.

path.moveAnchors.description: Moves the direct-selected anchors by dx, dy (whole paths when fully selected).

path.rectCut.description: Crops the selected paths to a rectangle as real geometry (not a clipping mask).

path.removeAnchor.description: Removes one anchor from a path and refits the curve around it.

path.removeAnchors.description: Removes the direct-selected anchors without opening their paths, refitting the curves.

path.reshape.description: Drags path id at a point by dx, dy as the Reshape tool does, with nearby anchors following on a smooth falloff.

path.reshapeSegment.description: Bends one segment so its point at parameter t moves by dx, dy.

path.reverse.description: Reverses the direction of the selected or given paths, or sets every subpath clockwise or counter-clockwise.

path.setAnchors.description: Replaces the whole geometry of path id with the given subpaths of anchors and handles.

path.setFillRule.description: Sets the fill rule (non-zero or even-odd) of the selected or given paths and compound paths.

path.setHandle.description: Moves the in or out direction handle of one anchor of path id to x, y, optionally breaking the handles' symmetry.

path.smoothRegion.description: Smooths the selected paths near a drag along points, reducing anchors; answers before and after anchor counts.

path.split.description: Splits a path at a segment parameter or an anchor: a closed path opens there, an open one becomes two; answers the ids.

pattern.delete.description: Deletes a pattern swatch; objects painted with it lose that paint.

pattern.list.description: Answers the document's patterns with their tile types and sizes, and which is being edited.

pattern.options.description: Sets a pattern's options: name, tile type, brick offset, size, spacing, overlap and editing display.

pattern.transform.description: Transforms only the placement of the selected objects' pattern paints by a matrix, leaving the objects.

pdf.preset.delete.description: Deletes a saved PDF preset (built-in ones stay).

pdf.preset.export.description: Writes PDF presets as a .vcpdfpresets file, or answers its text.

pdf.preset.import.description: Imports PDF presets from a .vcpdfpresets file.

pdf.preset.list.description: Answers the PDF presets, built-in and saved, with their descriptions and settings.

pdf.preset.save.description: Creates or changes a saved PDF preset from options; answers it.

perspective.attach.description: Projects the selected or given objects onto a perspective plane (default the active one).

perspective.draw.description: Runs a shape command and attaches the result to a perspective plane, snapping its corners to the gridlines.

perspective.editText.description: Shows type in perspective flat in isolation mode for editing; exiting isolation projects it again.

perspective.grid.define.description: Defines the perspective grid as the Define Grid dialog does: preset, kind, units, scale, gridlines, viewing angle and distance, horizon and colours.

perspective.grid.get.description: Answers the document's perspective grid model, its Define Grid fields and the station point.

perspective.grid.lock.description: Locks, unlocks or toggles the perspective grid's widgets; not an undo step.

perspective.grid.lockStation.description: Locks, unlocks or toggles the station point so dragging a vanishing point turns the viewing angle.

perspective.grid.preset.description: Resets the perspective grid to a 1-, 2- or 3-point preset fitted to the first artboard and shows it.

perspective.grid.rulers.description: Shows, hides or toggles the perspective grid's ruler.

perspective.grid.set.description: Merges settings into the document's perspective grid: kind, origin, horizon, vanishing points, distance, cell size, extent and plane offsets.

perspective.grid.show.description: Shows, hides or toggles the perspective grid; view state, not an undo step.

perspective.grid.snap.description: Turns snapping to the perspective gridlines on, off or toggles it.

perspective.move.description: Slides objects within their perspective plane (or along its normal) from one point to another, optionally as copies.

perspective.nudge.description: Nudges the selection in perspective by the keyboard increment, as the arrow keys do with the Perspective Selection tool.

perspective.plane.matchObject.description: Moves the plane an object is attached to onto the object and makes it the active plane.

perspective.plane.move.description: Moves a perspective plane along its normal, optionally moving or copying the objects on it.

perspective.plane.set.description: Sets the active perspective plane (left, right, ground or none) that drawing and attaching use; not an undo step.

perspective.presets.delete.description: Deletes a saved perspective grid preset.

perspective.presets.export.description: Writes perspective grid presets as a .vcperspective file, or answers its text.

perspective.presets.import.description: Imports perspective grid presets from a .vcperspective file.

perspective.presets.list.description: Answers the perspective grid presets, built-in and saved.

perspective.presets.save.description: Creates or changes a saved perspective grid preset.

perspective.release.description: Detaches objects from the perspective grid without changing their geometry.

perspective.transform.description: Transforms objects within their own perspective planes by a matrix in plane coordinates, with optional depth and copy.

perspective.widget.options.description: Shows or hides the Plane Switching Widget and sets its corner; with no params answers the settings.

plugin.info.description: Answers one plug-in's entry, manifest, defaults and last error.

plugin.install.description: Validates and installs a WebAssembly plug-in for this session from a file or bytes.

plugin.list.description: Answers the installed WebAssembly plug-ins (filters and live effects) with their parameters.

plugin.reload.description: Installs every plug-in module in a folder (default the Additional Plug-ins Folder), reporting failures.

plugin.remove.description: Uninstalls a plug-in; its live effects then leave the geometry as it is.

plugin.run.description: Runs an object-filter plug-in with parameters on the selected paths.

prefs.get.description: Answers one preference's value (or group), or all preferences.

prefs.list.description: Answers every preference with its key, category, label, kind and current value.

prefs.reset.description: Resets one preference category, or all preferences, to their defaults.

prefs.set.description: Sets one or more preferences after validating them (see prefs.list for keys and kinds).

print.presets.delete.description: Deletes a saved print preset ([Default] stays).

print.presets.export.description: Writes print presets as a .vcprintpresets file, or answers its text.

print.presets.import.description: Imports print presets from a .vcprintpresets file.

print.presets.list.description: Answers the print presets, [Default] first, with their settings and differences from it.

print.presets.save.description: Creates or changes a saved print preset.

print.preview.description: Answers the print layout the settings give: page count and each sheet's artboard, tile, size, orientation and scale.

print.setup.description: Sets the document's print settings: copies, artboards, media, orientation, scaling, tiling, marks, bleed, output and separations.

print.tiling.description: Answers the print pages as Show Print Tiling draws them, with their positions and numbers.

print.tiling.set.description: Places the print tiling origin (the first page's imageable area) or resets it.

recolor.apply.description: Recolours the selection in one undo step by a map of colour rows (from keys or hex to a new colour), with a tint method, an optional swatch library to snap to and a colour group to rewrite.

recolor.colors.description: Answers the unique colours the selection uses (fills, strokes, gradient stops, text, meshes, pattern tiles) with their keys, hex values and use counts, most used first; feed the keys to recolor.apply.

recolor.randomize.description: Answers a recolour map with the rows' new colours shuffled or their saturation and brightness randomised (seeded), without changing the document; pass it to recolor.apply.

recolor.reduce.description: Groups the selection's colours into a given number of rows of similar colours and answers the proposed map, without changing anything; pass the map to recolor.apply.

select.add.description: Adds the objects ids to the selection and answers the resulting selection.

select.all.description: Selects every unlocked, visible object (or all text while the Type tool edits) and answers the count.

select.allOnArtboard.description: Selects every object on the active (or given) artboard.

select.anchors.description: Sets, adds or toggles the direct selection of anchors (subpath and anchor indices) on path id.

select.anchorsMany.description: Sets, adds, toggles or subtracts direct-selected anchors on several paths at once.

select.editSaved.description: Renames or deletes saved selections in one undo step.

select.font.description: Selects the type objects that use a font family (and style); answers the count.

select.inverse.description: Selects every object that is not selected and deselects the others.

select.key.description: Makes one selected object the key object that Align aligns to and Distribute Spacing spaces from; no id clears it.

select.magicWand.description: Selects objects similar to object id by the Magic Wand settings (fill, stroke, weight, opacity, blend), replacing, adding to or subtracting from the selection; answers the count.

select.nextAbove.description: Selects the next object above the selected one in the stacking order.

select.nextBelow.description: Selects the next object below the selected one in the stacking order.

select.none.description: Clears the selection, deselecting every object, anchor and guide.

select.object.allOnSameLayers.description: Selects every object on the layers the selected objects are on.

select.object.areaText.description: Selects every area type object; answers the count.

select.object.bristleBrushStrokes.description: Selects every path with a bristle brush on its stroke; answers the count.

select.object.brushStrokes.description: Selects every path with a brush applied to its stroke; answers the count.

select.object.clippingMasks.description: Selects every clipping path in the document.

select.object.directionHandles.description: Direct-selects every anchor of the selected paths so all their handles show; answers the anchor count.

select.object.openPaths.description: Selects every open path in the document.

select.object.pointText.description: Selects every point type object; answers the count.

select.object.slices.description: Selects every user and object slice; answers the count.

select.object.strayPoints.description: Selects every stray point (a path with a single anchor), usually to delete them.

select.object.textObjects.description: Selects every type object in the document.

select.recall.description: Selects the objects of a saved selection (deleted ones are skipped); answers the count.

select.reselect.description: Repeats the last Select Same or Select Object command with the current selection.

select.same.appearance.description: Selects every object with the same appearance stack as the first selected object.

select.same.appearanceAttribute.description: Selects every object sharing one appearance attribute (a fill, stroke or effect) with the first selected object.

select.same.blendingMode.description: Selects every object with the first selected object's blending mode.

select.same.fillAndStroke.description: Selects every object with both the first selected object's fill and stroke colours.

select.same.fillColor.description: Selects every object filled with the first selected object's fill colour (tints of the same global swatch included).

select.same.fontFamily.description: Selects every type object in the first selected type's font family; answers the count.

select.same.fontFamilyStyle.description: Selects every type object in the first selected type's font family and style; answers the count.

select.same.fontFamilyStyleSize.description: Selects every type object with the first selected type's font family, style and size; answers the count.

select.same.fontSize.description: Selects every type object with the first selected type's font size; answers the count.

select.same.graphicStyle.description: Selects every object linked to the graphic style the first selected object is linked to.

select.same.opacity.description: Selects every object with the first selected object's opacity.

select.same.shapeType.description: Selects every live shape of the same kind as the first selected one (rectangles, ellipses, polygons).

select.same.strokeColor.description: Selects every object stroked with the first selected object's stroke colour.

select.same.strokeWeight.description: Selects every object with the first selected object's stroke weight.

select.same.symbolInstance.description: Selects every instance of the symbol the first selected instance uses; answers the count.

select.same.textFillColor.description: Selects every type object with the first selected type's text fill colour; answers the count.

select.same.textStrokeColor.description: Selects every type object with the first selected type's text stroke colour; answers the count.

select.save.description: Saves the current selection in the document under a name so select.recall can restore it; answers the name.

select.savedList.description: Answers the names of the active document's saved selections.

select.set.description: Replaces the selection with the objects ids and answers the resulting selection; most editing commands then act on it.

select.toggle.description: Toggles each of the objects id or ids in or out of the selection and answers the resulting selection.

shape.arc.description: Draws an arc from x1, y1 to x2, y2, open or closed; answers its id.

shape.ellipse.description: Draws an ellipse in the box x, y, width, height (optional rotation) with the current paint; answers its id.

shape.flare.description: Draws a lens flare (centre, halo, rays and rings) with the Flare tool's options; answers its id.

shape.line.description: Draws a straight line segment from x1, y1 to x2, y2 with the current stroke; answers its id.

shape.polarGrid.description: Draws a polar grid of concentric and radial dividers in a box as one group; answers its id.

shape.polygon.description: Draws a regular polygon with a centre, radius and number of sides; answers its id.

shape.rectangle.description: Draws a rectangle at x, y with width and height (optional corner radius and rotation about its centre) in the current layer with the current paint; answers its id.

shape.rectangularGrid.description: Draws a rectangular grid of rows and columns in a box as one group; answers its id.

shape.spiral.description: Draws a spiral with a centre, radius, decay and number of segments; answers its id.

shape.star.description: Draws a star with a centre, outer and inner radii and a number of points; answers its id.

shapeBuilder.merge.description: Merges (or erases) the regions a drag along points passes through, as the Shape Builder does; see shapeBuilder.regions for the regions.

shapeBuilder.regions.description: Answers the faces, line pieces and edges the Shape Builder sees among the selected or given paths, with their bounds and sources.

shaper.expand.description: Expands a Shaper group into ordinary paths of its visible result.

shaper.release.description: Releases a Shaper group back to its original paths.

shaper.scribble.description: Applies a Shaper tool scribble along points: removes fills, merges regions or erases stroke pieces of nearby art.

shaper.select.description: Selects a Shaper group then a face at a point, or enters construction isolation to select an original path.

slice.list.description: Answers the slices as laid out, numbered left to right and top to bottom, with their sources, rectangles and options.

stroke.set.description: Sets stroke options of the selection or ids: weight, cap, join, miter limit, alignment, dashes, arrowheads and width profile.

stroke.setAdvanced.description: Sets the Stroke panel's extras: arrowhead scale and swap, width-profile flip, and an art or pattern brush on the stroke.

stroke.widthPoint.copy.description: Copies a width point to another position along the stroke.

stroke.widthPoint.remove.description: Removes width points from a path's stroke; removing the last one leaves a uniform stroke.

stroke.widthPoint.set.description: Adds or moves a width point on a path's stroke at fraction t with left and right widths, as the Width tool does.

stroke.widthProfile.add.description: Saves the selected stroke's variable width as a named width profile in the profile list; answers its name.

stroke.widthProfile.delete.description: Removes a saved width profile from the list (built-ins can't be deleted); strokes keep their widths.

stroke.widthProfile.list.description: Answers the width profiles (built-in and saved) with their width points, and which one the selected stroke uses.

stroke.widthProfile.reset.description: Removes every saved width profile, keeping the built-in ones; answers how many were removed.

stroke.widthProfile.set.description: Sets a variable width profile on strokes as [t, left, right] factors, or null for a uniform stroke.

swatch.addUsedColors.description: Adds a swatch for each colour the art (or only the selection) uses, optionally global and linking the matching paints.

swatch.delete.description: Deletes swatches or colour groups by name in one undo step; art using a deleted global swatch keeps its colour unlinked.

swatch.duplicate.description: Duplicates a swatch under a new unique name.

swatch.edit.description: Changes a swatch: its name, colour or colour mode, global and spot flags, or replaces its paint; linked art updates.

swatch.editGroup.description: Rewrites a colour group's colours in order (adding or removing swatches as needed) and optionally renames it.

swatch.library.add.description: Adds swatches or colour groups from a library to the document's swatches, optionally applying the first to the selection.

swatch.library.copyToUser.description: Copies a loaded swatch library into the user library folder so it is listed every time the app starts.

swatch.library.get.description: Answers one swatch library's swatches and colour groups.

swatch.library.list.description: Answers every swatch library (built-in, user and loaded) with its category and swatch count.

swatch.library.load.description: Loads a swatch library file (.vcswatches, .gpl, .ase, .acb) or another document's swatches so the library panel lists it.

swatch.library.save.description: Saves the document's swatches as a library file (native JSON, GPL palette or ASE exchange), or answers the data.

swatch.list.description: Answers the document's swatches (colours, tints, gradients, patterns) with their kind, group, global/spot flags and colour values.

swatch.merge.description: Merges two or more solid swatches into the first; paints linked to the others relink to it.

swatch.move.description: Moves swatches (or colour groups) to a position or into another colour group.

swatch.new.description: Adds swatches from a colour, a list of colours, the current fill, a gradient, a pattern or a tint, optionally global or spot and in a group.
